title: Landscape visual evaluation and place attachment in historical and cultural districts: a study based on semantic differential scale and eye tracking experimental methods
research_question: This study investigates the relationships between Visual Attention (VA), demographic influences, and perceived landscape values (Aesthetic Value (AV) and Cultural Value (CV)) in historical and cultural districts, using eye-tracking (ET) technology and Semantic Differential (SD) scale to understand how different visitor demographics perceive these landscape elements.

participants.description: Visitors to Lijiang Old Town and Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, China. Sample included 203 males, 184 females; age groups: 18-35 (142), 36-55 (123), over 55 (122); nationality: Domestic (Chinese) (271), International (116); expertise: 97 heritage conservation or tourism experts, 290 non-experts.
participants.recruitment: Stratified sampling method, recruited from popular spots within Lijiang Old Town and Jade Dragon Snow Mountain.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Six distinctive photographs representing three landscape types: natural mountainous, historical town, and modern tourism infrastructure. Two photos per type. Images were iconic and sourced from official tourism websites.

mechanisms: Visual attention (VA) correlates with perceived landscape values (Aesthetic Value and Cultural Value).
Natural features attract immediate and sustained visual attention due to their inherent visual appeal and capacity to offer peace.
Cultural features, while attracting less immediate attention, are highly valued once noticed due to their historical depth and cultural integrity.
Demographic factors (age, gender, nationality, expertise) significantly influence how visitors perceive and value landscapes, leading to distinct visual attention and value assessment patterns.
Architectural features contribute to visual and emotional experience, particularly when conveying historical narratives or enhancing ambiance.
implementation_implications: Landscape managers and designers should focus on enhancing the significance of natural features and well-integrated architectural elements to drive VA and higher subjective value ratings.
Conservation efforts should prioritize engaging features to maintain or increase visitor satisfaction and engagement.
Tailor-made conservation and tourism management policies should consider demographic variations in landscape perception.
Improved cultural interpretation methods can assist foreign tourists in understanding and empathizing with cultural narratives and historical significance.
Aesthetically pleasing and culturally rich environments improve touristic interest and psychological place attachment.

limitations: Application of a laboratory environment for ET reduces ecological validity; future research should implement more dynamic and complete environments like virtual reality.
Findings cannot be generalized to different cultural and historically significant areas as research focused solely on two specific locations.

The study demonstrates correlations between ET metrics and human value reviews but neglects to investigate the underlying reasons for these relationships; future research should employ experimental methods to change specific landscape features and measure resulting impacts.
